dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) style; uses SCREEN SECTION with LINE/COL clauses, INDEXED file with named RECORD KEY syntax (CRN-KEY=ISAM-IO-KEY), relative file path strings, and IS INITIAL PROGRAM — all consistent with GnuCOBOL on a PC/Linux environment
evidence: RECORD KEY IS CRN-KEY=ISAM-IO-KEY CRN (GnuCOBOL named key syntax)

purpose.domain_detail: University course scheduling system (UAFS — University of Arkansas Fort Smith); adds records to a schedule master ISAM file
purpose.summary: SCHED-ADD is a batch/interactive program that allows a user to add a new course schedule record to an ISAM indexed file (SCHEDULE-MASTER.DAT). It reads the last-used CRN from a sequential file, increments it, collects course details via a screen form, confirms with the user, and writes the new record. The loop allows adding multiple records.

notable_features: INDEXED file with multiple ALTERNATE KEYs and named key syntax
LINE SEQUENTIAL organization for CRN counter file
REWRITE on sequential file for CRN counter update
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
verdict.notes: Comment header says BLDG-INQ.CBL but PROGRAM-ID is SCHED-ADD — likely copy-paste of header from another program in the same student project. The named RECORD KEY syntax (CRN-KEY=ISAM-IO-KEY) is GnuCOBOL-specific. REWRITE LAST-CRN (elementary item, not FD record) may be a student coding error. Overall this is a student university project.
